title: TTYL — Talk To You Later
subtitle: Claude Code plugin: live prompt-cache TTL in the status line, plus an optional Windows desktop tile that flashes when Claude finishes a turn
plain_subtitle: Knows when Claude is working vs. waiting, so you don't lose your speed-up cache or miss a finished reply

capabilities: Routes 5 lifecycle hooks through one script
jq optional — sed fallback when missing
plain_capabilities: Listens to five things Claude tells it
Remembers each chat in its own little file
Shows a coloured countdown in your status bar
Flips to spinning while Claude is working
Works even if your computer is missing extra tools

key_nodes.label: hooks.json
key_nodes.plain_label: The list of things to listen for
key_nodes.detail: Declares 5 lifecycle hooks → all route to cache-hooks.sh
key_nodes.plain_detail: Tells Claude Code to run our script whenever any of 5 things happen

key_nodes.label: cache-hooks.sh
key_nodes.plain_label: The script that writes the state
key_nodes.detail: Single entry point — branches on $hook_event_name and writes the per-session JSON
key_nodes.plain_detail: Decides what just happened and updates the chat's little file

key_nodes.label: cache-segment.sh
key_nodes.detail: Reads per-session JSON and prints ⊕⚫🔴 cache M:SS
key_nodes.plain_detail: Reads the file and prints the coloured countdown text

key_nodes.label: statusline-standalone.sh
key_nodes.detail: Composes cache-segment + model name | for users without a custom statusline
key_nodes.plain_detail: A ready-made status bar for people who don't have their own

key_nodes.label: ~/.claude/cache-timers/<sid>.json
key_nodes.detail: Per-session state — keyed by Claude's session_id, atomically rewritten on every event
key_nodes.plain_detail: Each Claude conversation gets its own tiny status file

key_nodes.label: ~/.claude/.cache-timestamp
key_nodes.detail: Single-file mirror — back-compat for status lines that don't pass session_id
key_nodes.plain_detail: An older shared file kept around so older setups still work

key_nodes.label: test_cache_hooks.sh
key_nodes.detail: Bash test harness — verifies every event writes the right state
key_nodes.plain_detail: Automated checks that prove the script behaves correctly

layers.plain_display_name: The floating timer on your screen
capabilities: Single floating tile with one row per active Claude session
Flashes the row when Claude finishes a turn (active → idle)
Click a row → focus the owning VSCode window
Yellow border on the row whose VSCode is foreground
Drag to move; persistent position; right-click menu
Pinned to the current Win11 virtual desktop every second
plain_capabilities: A small always-on-top window listing every active chat
Click a row to jump back to that VSCode window
Highlights the row for whichever VSCode you're using right now
Drag it anywhere; remembers where you put it
Follows you between Windows virtual desktops

key_nodes.detail: QApplication, tray icon, startup wiring; 1s timer pins the tile to the current vdesk
key_nodes.plain_detail: Starts the app, the tray icon, and the floating tile

key_nodes.label: CacheTimersWatcher
key_nodes.detail: Polls ~/.claude/cache-timers/ every 1s; emits added/updated/removed/replaced Qt signals

key_nodes.label: AggregateTile

steps.label: SessionStart fires
steps.detail: Claude opens a new chat — the SessionStart hook fires with session_id and cwd.
steps.plain_detail: The first thing that happens when you start chatting.

steps.label: Branch on event
steps.detail: case "$hook_event_name" picks the state to write. SessionStart → state=none.
steps.plain_detail: The script looks at what kind of thing just happened and reacts.

steps.label: Write state=none
steps.detail: atomic .json.tmp → mv pattern; one file per session_id, plus the legacy single-file mirror.
steps.plain_label: Save 'no cache yet' to the file
steps.plain_detail: The chat now has its own little status file.

steps.label: UserPromptSubmit fires
steps.detail: You submit a prompt — the cache is being refreshed for the next turn.
steps.plain_label: You hit enter on a prompt
steps.plain_detail: Now Claude is doing work — the cache is being topped up.

steps.label: Write state=active
steps.detail: PreCompact gets the same treatment so /compact also flips the indicator to active.
steps.plain_detail: The status file now says Claude is busy.

steps.label: Statusline reads file → 🔄 active
steps.detail: cache-segment.sh reads .state and prints the spinner pill while Claude works.
steps.plain_label: Status bar shows the spinning icon
steps.plain_detail: Your status bar now shows that Claude is working.

steps.label: Stop fires
steps.detail: Claude finishes its turn — cache was just refreshed, countdown begins.
steps.plain_detail: Claude is done thinking and writing for this turn.

steps.label: Write state=idle + epoch
steps.detail: Records 'idle:<unix_ts>' so the segment can compute remaining = TTL - (now - epoch).
steps.plain_detail: The file now records when Claude finished, so the countdown can start.

steps.label: Statusline shows 🟢 4:32 → 🟡 1:47 → 🔴
steps.detail: Segment recomputes every second; colour switches at 2:00 (yellow) and 1:00 (red), then 'expired'.
steps.plain_label: Countdown ticks down in your status bar
steps.plain_detail: You see the colour change as time runs out before the cache expires.

steps.label: Watcher poll detects change
steps.detail: CacheTimersWatcher polls the dir every 1s; emits session_updated when mtime changes.
steps.plain_detail: The floating tile is also reading the file and notices the update.

steps.label: TimerRow flashes (active → idle)
steps.detail: TimerState.is_finish_transition triggers the drop-shadow glow animation on the row.
steps.plain_label: The row flashes to grab your attention
steps.plain_detail: The little pill on screen lights up so you notice Claude is done.

steps.label: Click → vscode_finder.find_hwnd
steps.detail: Walks the recorded pid up the process tree to Code.exe; falls back to window-title match against cwd parts.
steps.plain_label: You click and it jumps to your editor
steps.plain_detail: Clicking the row brings the right VSCode window to the front.

steps.label: SessionEnd fires
steps.detail: Hook deletes ~/.claude/cache-timers/<sid>.json so the watcher promptly removes the row.
steps.plain_detail: The chat ends and the floating tile drops the row.

steps.label: jq missing? → sed fallback
steps.detail: If jq isn't on PATH, the script falls back to sed-based JSON extraction so default Git Bash on Windows still works.
steps.plain_label: If a tool is missing, use a backup
steps.plain_detail: The script can still read the data even on a basic computer setup.

steps.label: Watcher: psutil.pid_exists → evict
steps.detail: Hard kill / closed terminal means SessionEnd never fires. Watcher checks the recorded pid each scan and deletes the file when the owning process is gone.
steps.plain_label: Crashed chat? Quietly remove its row
steps.plain_detail: If a chat crashes, the floating tile cleans up after itself.
